comment: Instruction-level patches applied by the recompiler (tools/lib/codegen.mjs). Each one reads a runtime variable from runtime/src/recomp_rt.h; the variables default to values that reproduce the original instruction exactly.

spriteCull.comment: Sprite pieces are dropped unless (X - $60) <= $160 unsigned, i.e. screen x in [-32, 320]. These compares add patch_cull_left to the register value and patch_cull_widen to the limit, so widescreen keeps pieces in the side areas. The register itself is not changed.

cameraClamp.comment: Horizontal camera limits (sub at $00CF..): the camera x is clamped to [0, ($FF177A)]. These three instructions use cam_margin() instead, a runtime value that is 0 without widescreen, so the wider screen stops at the map edges too.

playerDamage.comment: The player's hit handler subtracts the damage from the current HP ($8A of the player object at $FF19E8) here. With patch_no_damage set (the infinite health cheat) the damage is 0, so even a hit bigger than the whole health bar cannot kill.

hitDamage.comment: A hit stores its damage in the target's object at $86 here (flags in the top 4 bits, damage in the low 12); every object's own handler later takes it off its HP ($8A) after its defence ($92). The attack power cheat (patch_attack) makes the damage 2x, 4x or a one-hit kill for any target but the player (hit_damage() in recomp_rt.h); 0 keeps the original. Keys are the pc, values the source operand.

playerSpeed.comment: The move-with-collision routine loads an object's movement for this tick ($72 x, $76 y, 16.16) here before stepping it through the map. For the player's object the move speed cheat scales it (player_move() in recomp_rt.h); 100 keeps the original. Keys are the pc, values the field.

randomDrop.comment: Where an item comes into the world: a broken object (chest, pot, enemy) loads its drop (+$8C, item << 8 | count; $8000 and up index the one-time table at $043830, left alone) at dropPc, and a map places an item on the ground from its script at placePc. The randomizer (random_drop() in recomp_rt.h) swaps the item for another of its kind, fixed by the seed and the place; 0 keeps the original.
